question: Why does a drop in estrogen after menopause put women at higher risk for bone fractures?

options.A: Low hormone levels make the kidneys excrete all available vitamin D.
options.B: Estrogen normally helps protect bone density by regulating bone remodeling.
options.C: Lack of estrogen causes muscles to pull too hard on the skeleton.
options.D: Postmenopausal women absorb excess calcium that crystallizes in joints.

explanation: Estrogen keeps bone-building cells active. When levels fall, bone breakdown starts winning the race, which can lead to osteoporosis over time.

question: Which way of taking misoprostol gets into the bloodstream the fastest?

options.A: Vaginal
options.B: Oral
options.C: Rectal
options.D: Sublingual

explanation: Placing the pills under the tongue (sublingual) lets them absorb super fast into the blood vessels right there in the mouth. Brilliant shortcut!

question: As a nurse, you receive new paracetamol expiring in 2026, but the shelf already has stock expiring in 2025. What should you do?

options.A: Place the 2025 stock in front and dispense it before the 2026 stock
options.B: Mix all the tablets together in one big container
options.C: Return both supplies immediately to the central medical store
options.D: Place the 2026 stock in front and keep the 2025 stock behind

explanation: Great clinical habit! Always use the ones expiring sooner (2025) so nothing spoils on the shelf. That's true nursing resourcefulness.

question: A client stopped taking her oral contraceptive pills because she kept forgetting daily doses. What is a great alternative to suggest?

options.A: Switching to a long-acting method like an implant or injection
options.B: Stopping all contraception permanently without alternatives
options.C: Taking three pills at once every Sunday morning
options.D: Relying entirely on calendar guessing without records

explanation: Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like implants or injections take the stress out of daily pill-taking!

question: What is the primary goal of leadership in community health practice?

options.A: Empowering communities to manage their own health
options.B: Reducing the operational costs of local clinics
options.C: Enforcing strict compliance with national hospital policies
options.D: Directing all medical treatment decisions without input

explanation: Community leadership focuses on working alongside the population so they can eventually direct and sustain their own health improvements. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h1)

question: How do birth spacing and family planning help break the cycle of anaemia?

options.A: They remove the need for postpartum hygiene care.
options.B: They stop babies from getting birth defects.
options.C: They cure genetic blood disorders.
options.D: They give the mother's body time to rebuild iron stores before the next pregnancy.

explanation: Giving the body time to recover between babies prevents mom's iron and nutrient levels from staying dangerously depleted.

question: A community health nurse wants to help a low-income mother boost her child's protein intake affordably. Which local combination works best?

options.A: Beans and corn or rice
options.B: Imported tinned foreign chocolates
options.C: Pure refined table sugar and water
options.D: Bottled carbonated soft drinks

explanation: Pairing beans with grains like corn or rice is a classic, budget-friendly way to serve complete protein that supports healthy childhood growth.

question: What is a common behavioral sign that someone might be struggling with drug abuse?

options.A: Consistent attendance at routine clinical check-ups
options.B: Sleeping uninterrupted for eight hours each night
options.C: Sudden personality changes and withdrawal from family activities
options.D: Eating balanced meals at regular hours every single day

explanation: Watch out for secrecy, sudden mood swings, and a person pulling away from family and friends. You're learning to spot the clinical signs!

question: Why do we advise pregnant mothers to eat small, frequent meals instead of three massive plates of food?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood sugar during the afternoon
options.B: To speed up the absorption of prenatal vitamins into the bloodstream
options.C: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and putting pressure on the sphincter
options.D: To stop the liver from producing excess bile during digestion

explanation: Smaller meals keep tummy pressure low, stopping acid from splashing up into the food pipe.

question: Why are the veins in the lower part of the oesophagus so critical during liver disease?

options.A: They prevent stomach acid from washing backward into the throat.
options.B: They supply the main nerve impulses that trigger swallowing waves.
options.C: They carry all arterial blood returning from the entire stomach.
options.D: They form a direct connection between portal and systemic veins.

explanation: Well done! Because these veins link the liver's portal system to the general body circulation, they can bulge and bleed dangerously when liver scarring blocks blood flow.

question: How often should an antenatal clinic see a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease during her first two trimesters?

options.A: Every two weeks
options.B: Only in emergencies
options.C: Twice a week
options.D: Once every month

explanation: Spot on. High-risk pregnancies need close monitoring right from the start—usually every two weeks to catch any problems early.

question: Which ethical principle simply means the duty to do no harm to your patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Non-maleficence
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Non-maleficence is just a big word for a simple rule: do no harm. As a nurse, you always make sure your actions or mistakes don't cause unnecessary pain or suffering.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent leaving items inside a patient?

options.A: Rushing through the final count to finish quickly
options.B: Using standardized hospital safety checklists
options.C: Minimizing operating room noise during counts
options.D: Encouraging open communication among staff

explanation: Never rush a count! Taking your time, staying calm, and keeping the room quiet helps catch errors.

question: What is the main reason food holds such deep meaning in many religions?

options.A: Religious leaders mandate specific daily calorie requirements
options.B: It is closely tied to spiritual meanings, purity laws, and traditions
options.C: Diets were strictly designed to prevent infectious diseases
options.D: Ancient societies lacked basic knowledge of food preservation

explanation: Religious diets aren't just about nutrition science—they are deeply rooted in sacred commands, purity concepts, and passing down traditions through generations.

question: How do subjective ways of knowing (like personal feelings) differ from structured ways of knowing?

options.A: Subjective ways are guaranteed to be 100 percent accurate
options.B: Structured ways are only used by doctors, never by nurses
options.C: Structured ways cannot be used in a hospital setting
options.D: Subjective ways rely more on personal feelings and habits rather than testing

explanation: Subjective knowing is often based on gut feeling or tradition. Structured methods, on the other hand, use careful testing to prove what works.

question: Which question is most important when a nurse wants to understand a patient's risk for regional nutritional problems?

options.A: Where do you get your daily food, and what crops grow in your home area?
options.B: What brand of cooking oil do your neighbors buy?
options.C: How many rooms are in your house in the city?
options.D: What is your family ancestry?

explanation: Asking about a patient's food sources and farming background helps you spot environmental risks for specific vitamin or mineral deficiencies.

question: Why is family planning counseling considered such an important part of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: It cures underlying pelvic inflammatory disease without antibiotics
options.B: It stops all immediate bleeding from uterine perforation
options.C: It helps women prevent another unwanted pregnancy in the near future
options.D: It is required by law to permanently sterilize every female patient

explanation: Spot on! Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion, so giving timely contraceptive advice helps prevent repeat unsafe procedures.

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing routine on two existing hospital wards without disrupting shift schedules. Which design fits best?

options.A: Quasi-experimental design
options.B: Historical research design
options.C: Phenomenological design
options.D: True experimental design

explanation: Spot on! When you have to use existing groups (like pre-formed wards) instead of mixing everyone randomly, you are doing a quasi-experiment.

question: An infusion pump starts beeping with a 'downstream occlusion' alarm. What should you check first?

options.A: The software version installed on the pump display
options.B: The IV tubing for kinks, closed clamps, or blockages
options.C: The main hospital electrical breaker panel in the hallway
options.D: The expiration date printed on the primary medication bag

explanation: That's correct! 'Downstream' means between the pump and the patient. Always check the line first for bends, pinches, or a closed roller clamp.

question: What does a high Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) usually tell you about a patient?

options.A: Excessive bone mineral density
options.B: Decreased red blood cell production
options.C: Active inflammation or infection
options.D: Low dietary calcium intake

explanation: When there is inflammation in the body, certain proteins make red blood cells stick together and fall faster in a test tube. That speeds up the ESR! Spotting this helps you catch inflammation early.

question: What is a core responsibility of a community health nurse working with nurseries?

options.A: Managing the financial profits and tax returns of the facility
options.B: Replacing the parents as the primary legal guardian
options.C: Purchasing all commercial toys and playground equipment
options.D: Conducting health appraisals and checking immunization records

explanation: Community health nurses focus on health promotion, disease prevention, and monitoring vaccination compliance in childcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which embryonic germ layer gives rise to the nervous system and skin?

options.A: Trophoblast
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: Think 'ecto' for outer—the outer layer builds things that face the outside world, like your skin and your brain/nerves!

question: How does acute physical or emotional stress falsely affect a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: It destroys red blood cells and ruins the laboratory blood samples
options.B: It releases hormones like adrenaline and cortisol that raise blood sugar
options.C: It slows down digestion so the stomach cannot absorb the glucose drink
options.D: It forces the pancreas to release too much insulin, causing severe hypoglycemia

explanation: Stress hormones mobilize stored energy and push blood glucose levels up, which can mimic diabetes during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why is mixing local herbal mixtures with modern hospital drugs a hidden danger during self-medication?

options.A: Herbal mixtures are always chemically identical to factory-made pills
options.B: Herbs always taste too bitter to swallow with tablets
options.C: Unregulated herbs may contain hidden drugs that cause harmful interactions
options.D: Modern drugs completely destroy the healing power of leaves

explanation: You got it! Local mixtures often have active chemical ingredients that clash unpredictably with your hospital prescription.

question: How should the little prongs of a nasal cannula face when you put them into a patient's nose?

options.A: Flattened sideways
options.B: Pointing straight up
options.C: Curving downward
options.D: Tilted backward

explanation: They are shaped to match human anatomy! Pointing them downward ensures they slide comfortably along the natural curve of the nasal passages.

question: What makes evacuating a sick patient off a ship so tricky and dangerous?

options.A: Excessive paperwork required by land-based police
options.B: The legal prohibition of helicopters over international waters
options.C: Adverse weather and difficult transfer conditions at sea
options.D: Lack of any communication tools between ship and shore

explanation: Spot on! Shifting waves and high winds make moving a patient via helicopter hoist or between two moving boats extremely risky.

question: Who starts the whole disease-reporting chain right at the grassroots level?

options.A: The administrative clerk in charge of billing
options.B: The frontline nurse or doctor who assesses the patient
options.C: The international health organization representative
options.D: The federal minister of health in the capital city

explanation: That's you! The nurse or clinician at the bedside or clinic floor who first sees the patient is always the crucial first link in the reporting chain.

question: Why must a nurse use a filter needle when drawing medication from a glass ampoule?

options.A: To make the plunger move more smoothly inside the barrel
options.B: To filter out bacteria present in the room air
options.C: To change the chemical pH of the liquid medicine
options.D: To prevent tiny glass shards from entering the syringe

explanation: Snapping the neck of a glass ampoule creates microscopic shards. A filter needle traps these fragments so they are not injected into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the core golden rule behind standard precautions in nursing?

options.A: Treating all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious
options.B: Sterilizing disposable plastic syringes for reuse
options.C: Isolating only patients with confirmed laboratory diagnoses
options.D: Using gloves only when blood is visibly dripping

explanation: Standard precautions mean we treat every patient's blood and body fluids as if they could carry an infection. Safety first, always!

question: What is the safest way to handle a used injection needle?

options.A: Break the needle off the syringe by hand
options.B: Drop it immediately into a puncture-resistant sharps container
options.C: Recap it firmly using both hands before walking away
options.D: Place it inside a regular plastic waste bin

explanation: You've got it! Never mess around with used needles. Drop them straight into the sharps box to avoid accidental pricks.

question: What is the main goal of antimicrobial stewardship programs in hospitals?

options.A: Lowering hospital cleaning budgets by reducing soap purchases
options.B: Optimizing the use of anti-infectives to reduce resistance and harm
options.C: Ensuring every patient receives intravenous drugs automatically
options.D: Eliminating the need for laboratory cultures completely

explanation: Antimicrobial stewardship is all about using the right drug, at the right dose, for the right time—protecting patients from side effects and stopping superbugs from forming.

question: What is the biggest danger of carelessly throwing away used sharps?

options.A: Blockage of municipal drainage and sewage pipes
options.B: Transmission of blood infections through accidental pricks
options.C: Creation of unpleasant odors in hospital wards
options.D: Attraction of rodents and insects to the facility

explanation: A stray needle can pierce the skin and directly introduce infections like Hepatitis or HIV into a healthcare worker's bloodstream. Be careful out there! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why should you always encourage a patient on a high-protein diet to drink plenty of water?

options.A: It replaces the electrolytes lost through the skin
options.B: It slows down the digestion of amino acids in the stomach
options.C: It helps the kidneys clear extra nitrogen waste products
options.D: It prevents the patient from feeling hungry too often

explanation: Breaking down proteins produces urea and nitrogen waste that pass through the kidneys. Extra fluids protect the kidneys from working too hard and prevent dehydration!

question: Which mental health condition is most commonly seen in survivors of severe trauma and violence?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression
options.B: Attention deficit disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Seasonal affective disorder

explanation: Going through life-threatening violence leaves deep mental scars, frequently leading to what we call PTSD.

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation measures final impact
options.B: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always free
options.C: Monitoring happens after the project, while evaluation happens before
options.D: Monitoring is done by villagers, while evaluation is done by politicians

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously during the project to guide steps, while evaluation assesses overall results at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the main goal of Maternal and Child Health (MCH) services?

options.A: To provide free surgical procedures for aging populations
options.B: To reduce preventable illness and death in mothers and children
options.C: To manage chronic diseases in older adults
options.D: To replace traditional birth practices completely

explanation: You got this! MCH services are specially designed to protect and support the health and survival of mothers and young children. Every win starts with knowing your core goal!

question: When you are checking if a patient is fully 'oriented,' what three key things do you ask about?

options.A: Sight, hearing, and touch
options.B: Height, weight, and age
options.C: Pulse, temperature, and blood pressure
options.D: Person, place, and time

explanation: Checking person, place, and time is the classic, quick way to test if a patient's brain is alert and aware of their surroundings.

question: Which healthcare professional is an expert at helping a stroke patient relearn how to swallow and speak?

options.A: Clinical dietitian
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Hospital social worker

explanation: Speech-language pathologists are wonderful allies who specialize in helping patients recover their communication and safe swallowing skills after a brain injury.

question: Which of these common grains naturally contains gluten?

options.A: Sorghum
options.B: Rice
options.C: Millet
options.D: Barley

explanation: Barley is one of the main grains that naturally contains gluten, along with wheat and rye. You've got this!

question: Which blood test results shoot up when liver cells are actively inflamed or damaged?

options.A: Red blood cell count and hemoglobin
options.B: Serum sodium and potassium
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine
options.D: ALT and AST

explanation: Easy to remember: ALT and AST are special enzymes stored inside liver cells. When those cells get injured, the enzymes leak out into the bloodstream.

question: What is the main job of first-pass metabolism in the liver?

options.A: To process and filter digested nutrients, toxins, and drugs before they reach the rest of the body
options.B: To manufacture red blood cells using iron absorbed from dietary sources
options.C: To cool down ingested food before it circulates to sensitive brain tissues
options.D: To pump oxygen-rich blood directly from the digestive tract into the right side of the heart

explanation: The liver acts as the body's ultimate gatekeeper! Everything absorbed from our gut passes through first so the liver can filter out toxins and process nutrients before they travel anywhere else.

question: Which food must be strictly avoided by a patient taking a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)?

options.A: Fresh green leafy vegetables
options.B: Plain boiled white rice
options.C: Pasteurized cow's milk
options.D: Aged cheeses and cured meats

explanation: You got it! These foods are high in tyramine, which can trigger a dangerous, life-threatening spike in blood pressure when combined with MAOIs.

question: How is a research report different from a regular story essay?

options.A: It avoids using references or formal citations
options.B: It relies heavily on empirical data and structured formatting
options.C: It is always written in the first person narrative style
options.D: It focuses primarily on fictional clinical scenarios

explanation: Think of a research report as a neat, structured map of proven facts rather than a casual diary entry. You're doing great!

question: How many traditional 'rights' make up the golden rules of safe drug administration?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Seven
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Think of the classic five: right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, and right time. Master these, and you're well on your way!

question: How does school management help promote health teaching in the classroom?

options.A: By banning discussions about personal hygiene and nutrition
options.B: By ensuring health education is properly timetabled and resourced
options.C: By personally teaching every biology class in the school
options.D: By leaving health teaching entirely up to extracurricular clubs

explanation: Spot on! Management sets up the timetable and supplies the learning materials so teachers can teach health topics effectively.

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for surveillance in developing health systems?

options.A: Having too many computers on every hospital ward
options.B: Too many laboratories producing identical test results
options.C: Shortages of trained laboratory personnel and testing supplies
options.D: Excessive funding that overwhelms the management staff

explanation: Limited resources and trained staff make tracking and confirming infections much harder. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: How does the VAPP Act change how society and the law view domestic abuse within homes?

options.A: It turns domestic abuse into a punishable criminal offense.
options.B: It leaves punishment to traditional village elders.
options.C: It requires financial compensation without any legal trial.
options.D: It treats domestic abuse as a private family dispute.

explanation: Well done! Domestic abuse is no longer seen as a mere 'family secret' or private affair—it is a crime with legal consequences.

question: What is the main weak point of using the range to measure how spread out data is?

options.A: It can only be used with nominal data categories
options.B: It is easily distorted by a single extreme outlier
options.C: It requires complex calculus to calculate properly
options.D: It ignores the middle values of the dataset entirely

explanation: You're doing great! Because the range only looks at the absolute highest and lowest numbers, just one weird or extreme score can completely throw off the result.

question: What kind of conflict happens entirely inside your own head?

options.A: Intrapersonal conflict
options.B: Intragroup conflict
options.C: Intergroup conflict
options.D: Interpersonal conflict

explanation: Intrapersonal conflict is that inner battle we all face—like when you're trying to make a tough personal choice or dealing with stress all by yourself.

question: A patient arrives at your clinic with a long-term cough, heavy night sweats, and sudden weight loss. What should you do first?

options.A: Placing the patient in isolation precautions
options.B: Scheduling an immediate abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Checking the patient for peripheral edema
options.D: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Safety first! Those classic signs point right to TB, so your immediate priority is protecting everyone else in the clinic by isolating the patient.

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: What does a drug's half-life represent in pharmacokinetics?

options.A: The time it takes for the body to absorb half of an oral dose
options.B: The time it takes for blood concentration of the drug to decrease by 50 percent
options.C: The exact number of hours a drug remains active in the stomach
options.D: The time required for the liver to metabolize half of the active ingredient

explanation: Half-life measures how long it takes for the amount of drug in the blood to drop down to half of its previous level. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why must bed sheets in a hospital stay completely free of wrinkles?

options.A: Wrinkles make it difficult for the patient to adjust their pillows
options.B: Wrinkles signal to visitors that the nursing staff is careless
options.C: Wrinkles trap trapped air and cause the room temperature to rise
options.D: Wrinkles increase friction and pressure on the skin, leading to sores

explanation: You got it! Smooth sheets protect your patient's skin by preventing friction and pressure points that cause painful bedsores.

question: A nurse manager suddenly sees patient admissions double overnight. Which budgeting phase does this affect the most?

options.A: Historical auditing of past years
options.B: Initial executive board selection
options.C: Implementation and monitoring
options.D: Capital equipment depreciation

explanation: This happens during the live implementation phase, where managers constantly watch real-time patient numbers and adjust on the fly!

question: What symptom is most characteristic of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)?

options.A: Chronic constipation
options.B: Severe right shoulder pain
options.C: Heartburn
options.D: Projectile vomiting of blood

explanation: You've got it! Heartburn—that burning discomfort right behind your breastbone caused by acid irritation—is the classic hallmark of GORD.

question: Why do patients on blood thinners still rely on their body's natural healing to clear old clots?

options.A: Natural defenses are permanently shut down by the drugs
options.B: Medications destroy platelets before they reach the clot
options.C: Anticoagulants lack the ability to break down established fibrin
options.D: Anticoagulants only slow down the heart rate

explanation: Anticoagulants prevent new trouble, but breaking down existing clots is a job for the body's own natural cleaning system! Great job reviewing this.

question: What simple tool do community health nurses use to quickly screen children for acute malnutrition?

options.A: Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) tape
options.B: Sphygmomanometer and stethoscope
options.C: Urinary test strips for glucose
options.D: A standard household measuring tape

explanation: Spot on! The MUAC tape is a nurse's best friend in the field—it's quick, easy, and gives a reliable check on a child's wasting status. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is a major focus when caring for a fistula patient BEFORE her surgery?

options.A: Applying heavy makeup to distract from the patient's visible sadness
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately after the initial medical diagnosis
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the bladder completely dry
options.D: Improving nutritional status and treating any active infections

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition helps tissues heal much faster, and clearing infections ensures the body is ready for surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological mechanism that causes pressure injuries to form over bony prominences?

options.A: Excessive surface sweat softens the outer skin layer until it tears
options.B: Prolonged pressure cuts off capillary blood flow, causing tissue ischemia
options.C: Bacterial growth multiplies rapidly inside healthy sweat glands
options.D: The body's immune system attacks normal skin cells by mistake

explanation: When external pressure exceeds normal capillary pressure, blood flow stops, starving the tissues of oxygen and nutrients and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is the main reason for plotting a child's weight on a growth chart during clinic visits?

options.A: To check if the child needs immediate dental surgery
options.B: To calculate the exact adult height of the child
options.C: To determine how much money the family earns
options.D: To detect faltering growth early before severe malnutrition develops

explanation: Spot on! Growth charts let us catch weight drops or slow growth early so we can step in long before severe malnutrition sets in.

question: Around which week of pregnancy do hCG levels usually hit their highest peak?

options.A: Around the tenth week
options.B: Right after delivery of the placenta
options.C: At the moment of fertilization
options.D: Just before active labor begins

explanation: That's right! hCG shoots up super fast in the early weeks and peaks right around week ten before starting to drop down.

question: Which physical sign do nurses check first to quickly spot possible anaemia?

options.A: Swelling in the upper eyelids
options.B: Yellow color in the eyes
options.C: Pallor of the inner eyelids and nail beds
options.D: Dryness of the outer ears

explanation: Looking at the conjunctiva and nail beds is a quick, classic nursing trick to check if blood color looks healthy and pink!

question: Why is it best for nurses to avoid using extreme scare tactics when talking to teens about drugs?

options.A: Teens prefer lectures over friendly conversations
options.B: Exaggerated warnings are required by medical law
options.C: Teenagers see right through exaggerated claims and may lose trust in the nurse
options.D: Scare tactics instantly cure physical dependence within hours

explanation: Correct! Exaggerated warnings destroy your credibility. Teens spot fake claims easily, and once they lose trust, they stop listening altogether.

question: As a nurse explaining a treatment plan, what should you avoid doing?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient does not understand
options.B: Ensuring the conversation remains strictly confidential
options.C: Explaining the importance of abstaining from sex during treatment
options.D: Asking the patient about her current sexual partners

explanation: Always keep it simple! Heavy medical grammar just confuses patients. Talk to them in clear, everyday language they can easily grasp.

question: What makes the measuring tape especially useful for community health nursing?

options.A: It can diagnose complex infectious diseases
options.B: It is portable, cheap, and non-invasive
options.C: It provides automated digital health records
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: Field tools must be easy to carry and simple to use without hurting the patient, making basic tape measures ideal for outreach work. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: What does the presence of thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid usually indicate?

options.A: Rapid dilation of the maternal cervix
options.B: A normal and healthy progression of labour
options.C: Normal kidney function in a full-term baby
options.D: Previous foetal stress and bowel relaxation

explanation: Hypoxia relaxes the foetal anal sphincter, causing the baby to pass meconium into the amniotic fluid before delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h3)

question: What is the main public health approach used to control schistosomiasis in heavily affected communities?

options.A: Widespread daily chlorine spraying of all farmlands
options.B: Mandatory quarantine of all infected families
options.C: Mass drug administration of praziquantel
options.D: Surgical removal of adult worms from patients

explanation: Instead of waiting for individuals to fall sick, health teams treat whole communities—especially school children—all at once to knock down the disease burden. Brilliant public health strategy!

question: When opening a sterile pack, which part of the sterile drape or wrapper is always considered contaminated?

options.A: The portion closest to the patient
options.B: The top surface facing upwards
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The exact center of the drape

explanation: Spot on! That outer edge touches non-sterile surfaces when packaged, so we always treat the outer one-inch margin as unsterile.

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely *only* on the p-value when deciding to change how patients are cared for?

options.A: Hospital administrators only look at qualitative nurse interviews
options.B: Journal articles often hide the actual t-statistic value
options.C: P-values cannot be trusted when sample sizes are large
options.D: Statistical significance does not guarantee meaningful clinical impact

explanation: Just because a finding is statistically 'real' doesn't mean it makes a big enough difference to change everyday bedside nursing practice. Always look at the clinical picture!

question: Why does pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) raise a woman's risk of having an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Hormonal imbalances stop the uterine lining from growing
options.B: Scar tissue blocks and damages the fallopian tubes
options.C: Infection prevents the ovaries from releasing eggs
options.D: Bacteria destroy the muscular walls of the uterus

explanation: When PID heals, it leaves behind scar tissue that narrows the tubes. If a fertilized egg gets stuck in that narrow, scarred tube, it implants right there instead of the uterus.

question: How is menopause officially diagnosed in a patient?

options.A: Surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.C: Complete stop of pituitary hormones
options.D: Twelve straight months without a menstrual period

explanation: You got it! Clinicians look back and confirm menopause once a woman has gone a full 12 months without any bleeding.

question: Why should nurses care about the mental health of patients with visible skin problems?

options.A: Depression automatically cures the skin condition
options.B: Mental distress stops creams from absorbing
options.C: Psychological issues prevent any infections
options.D: Emotional stress can worsen physical skin flare-ups

explanation: Great thinking! The mind and skin are closely linked, so stress and anxiety can actually make skin rashes worse.

question: What is one of the main roles of a community health nurse in an intersectoral team?

options.A: Acting as a bridge connecting community members with other developmental sectors
options.B: Managing hospital budgets for the entire state health ministry
options.C: Taking over the administrative duties of local government chairpersons
options.D: Constructing boreholes and building roads without outside assistance

explanation: Right! Nurses serve as the vital link between health needs and sectors like water, education, and agriculture to solve problems together.

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: A subdermal hormonal implant
options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal foam applied before sex
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI during clinical assessments?

options.A: To screen for potential weight-related health risks
options.B: To determine exact daily caloric requirements
options.C: To diagnose specific cardiovascular diseases
options.D: To directly measure total body fat percentage

explanation: Great job! BMI is a quick, handy screening tool to flag weight categories that might put a patient at health risk, even though it doesn't measure fat directly.

question: Which hormone, released when you are under long-term stress, tends to lower your immune response?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Well done! High cortisol from chronic stress acts like a brake on your immune system, which is why stressed students easily catch colds during exams!

question: What fluid should you use to flush the IV tubing after a blood transfusion is complete?

options.A: Plain Tap Water
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose Water
options.D: Sterile Water for Injection

explanation: A normal saline flush nicely clears out any remaining blood products from the line without harming the patient's cells.

question: Where do the majority of the lymphatic vessels of the breast drain?

options.A: Cervical lymph nodes
options.B: Axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Mediastinal nodes
options.D: Inguinal lymph nodes

explanation: About 75% of breast lymph fluid drains into the axillary lymph nodes located in the armpit area. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h6)

question: Why is recording an accurate pregnancy history so important for an expectant mother?

options.A: It guarantees that she will not experience any surgical complications.
options.B: It proves whether her previous babies were born with birth defects.
options.C: It identifies if her past pregnancies put her at a higher medical risk now.
options.D: It determines the exact date of conception for the current pregnancy.

explanation: Knowing the exact number of past viable births helps the healthcare team prepare for potential issues tied to many previous pregnancies, such as bleeding or placental problems.

question: Which healthcare team members usually spend the most time providing direct, hands-on daily care to residents?

options.A: Certified Nursing Assistants
options.B: Physician specialists
options.C: Registered Dietitians
options.D: Hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! CNAs are the bedside backbone of long-term care, spending the most hours helping residents with daily needs.

question: When should instruments be checked for cleanliness and damage?

options.A: Directly after removal from the autoclave
options.B: Only when the surgeon complains about a tool
options.C: As soon as the items arrive dirty from the ward
options.D: After cleaning and before packaging

explanation: Staff inspect instruments right after they are washed and dried. This ensures no hidden dirt or broken parts slip through before they are wrapped up.

question: Where do most nutrient pollutants like nitrogen and phosphorus in water bodies come from?

options.A: Thermal discharge from power plants
options.B: Dissolved heavy metal mining
options.C: Agricultural fertilizer runoff
options.D: Floating physical plastic waste

explanation: Spot on! Fertilizers wash off farmlands during rains and flow into nearby streams and lakes, causing massive weed and algae growth.

question: Who produces the majority of domestic food supply in Nigeria?

options.A: Importing syndicates
options.B: Multinational corporations
options.C: Smallholder farmers
options.D: State-owned plantations

explanation: Small-scale local farmers do most of the primary growing and harvesting that feeds the nation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h2)

question: What do we call wound drainage that is clear and watery?

options.A: Sanguineous
options.B: Fibrinous
options.C: Purulent
options.D: Serous

explanation: Serous fluid comes from plasma—think of the clear liquid you see in a minor blister. Easy terminology to lock down!

question: A Muslim patient admitted during Ramadan needs medication three times a day with food. What should you do first?

options.A: Withhold all medications until the holy month of Ramadhan ends
options.B: Crush the medication and mix it into the patient's intravenous fluids
options.C: Insist that the patient break their religious fast immediately to take the pills
options.D: Collaborate with the care team to adjust medication timings around the fasting schedule

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Always talk with the doctor and pharmacist to safely schedule meds for non-fasting hours during Ramadan whenever possible.

question: Why must nurses gently correct unverified medication myths with pregnant patients?

options.A: Fear of medication often leads patients to stop vital treatments for chronic illnesses
options.B: Myths alter the pharmacokinetic absorption rate of oral vitamins
options.C: Misinformation causes the placenta to immediately reject all chemical agents
options.D: Patients will otherwise report the nurse to regulatory boards

explanation: When patients are scared by bad info, they might stop taking life-saving medicines. Clear, warm teaching keeps both mom and baby healthy!

question: Why are offline hobbies and sports so effective in preventing phone addiction?

options.A: It completely destroys the internal components of digital devices
options.B: It provides alternative sources of fulfillment and reduces reliance on virtual rewards
options.C: It prevents the eyes from ever blinking during daylight hours
options.D: It ensures the teenager never learns how to use modern computers

explanation: Real-world fun like sports, art, or hanging out with friends gives the brain natural satisfaction and connection, making us less glued to our phones.

question: Which method of applying a painful stimulus is usually avoided in modern nursing because it causes unnecessary bruising?

options.A: Supraorbital pressure
options.B: Trapezius squeeze
options.C: Nail bed pressure
options.D: Sternal rub

explanation: Vigorous sternal rubbing (grinding knuckles on the chest bone) can leave nasty bruises and trauma. Safer methods like a trapezius squeeze are preferred today.

question: Where does Community-Based Rehabilitation mainly take place?

options.A: A secure psychiatric asylum
options.B: A large federal teaching hospital
options.C: The local community and family home
options.D: A private overseas medical facility

explanation: Spot on! Community-Based Rehabilitation brings care straight to the patient's doorstep, helping them feel right at home with their loved ones and neighbours.
